subject: Sizing ask: Dedicated GPUs for 70B model (32k context) — KV cache + quantization impact
messages:
From: Sara Morris <sara.morris@vitalitherapeutics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Vitali Tech Ops <ops@vitalitherapeutics.com>

Subject: Dedicated sizing for 70B model (32k) — what do we need?

Hi Logan,

Quick intro — I'm Sara (ML infra lead) at Vitali Therapeutics. We're piloting a clinical assistant that uses a customer-tuned 70B model with 32k context for long patient notes. We're moving toward a production Dedicated capacity contract and need a sizing recommendation tied to expected throughput and quantization options.

Questions:
- For a 70B model with 32k context, what is the per-replica GPU requirement (A100/H100 80GB sizing assumptions ok)?
- How much KV cache memory should we budget per active request for 32k context?
- How does quantizing to 8-bit / 4-bit affect whether we can serve on 1x80GB vs needing multi-GPU model parallel?
- Given expected QPS: 4 sustained r/s with occasional spikes to 12 r/s, avg generation length ~512 tokens, what would you recommend for a Dedicated pool (replicas, headroom for canary/HA)?

Attached: small export of a sample session and token length distribution (kv-cache-estimates.csv). We'd like a short write-up we can use internally to align procurement and infra.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call.

—Sara Morris
ML Infra Lead, Vitali Therapeutics
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing for 70B model (32k) — what do we need?

Sara — thanks for the details and the sample session. Short answer up front: the delta between FP16 and aggressive 4-bit quantization is material — it can change whether one replica fits on a single 80GB GPU. Below I sketch two practical deployment options and a rough Dedicated pool recommendation given your QPS.

Assumptions I used (callouts so you can validate):
- Model: ~70B parameters.
- Baseline weight size (FP16) ~= 70B * 2 bytes ≈ 140 GB. That is the raw parameter footprint before activation / optimizer/overhead.
- KV cache scales with context length; for this class of model we use a conservative ballpark of ~0.8–1.0 KB per token for the key+value state (this captures hidden dim + layer count / KV packing). For 32k context that maps to roughly 25–32 MB per active request (per-token multiplier -> 32k * 0.9 KB ≈ 29MB). Note: KV is per-active-request and can accumulate if you keep many concurrent long-lived sessions.

Options:
1) FP16 single-replica (no quant):
   - Weights alone (~140 GB) exceed a single 80GB GPU. In practice you need model sharding across GPUs. With activation/serving overhead and KV for long context, we estimate ~180–200 GB of resident device memory required per replica, so plan for model-parallel replicas using 3x80GB GPUs (we've seen 2–3 GPU sharding depending on runtime optimizations).

2) Aggressive quant (4-bit / q4_f16-like):
   - Quantization can cut the on-device weight footprint by ~2.5–3.5x depending on algorithm (GPTQ/awq/lora-aware variants vary). Conservatively: weights -> ~40–60 GB. With KV for 32k (~30MB) and runtime overhead, a single 80GB GPU can host one replica of the quantized model with some room for batch headroom. That turns a 3-GPU replica into a single-GPU replica and reduces per-replica infra cost significantly.

Throughput sizing (given your targets: sustained 4 r/s, bursts to 12 r/s, avg gen = 512 tokens):
- Avg token work per request matters more than just QPS. With an avg generation of 512 tokens, each request will also stream back tokens, holding KV state for that session during generation.
- For conservative HA and canary: recommend 2 replicas for baseline (hot) + 1 canary/standby replica = 3 total active replicas. If you choose FP16 sharded replicas, that maps to 3 * (3x80GB) = 9 GPUs in the pool. If you choose quantized single-GPU replicas, 3 replicas ≈ 3 * (1x80GB) = 3 GPUs.

Recommendation summary:
- If you require exact FP16 inference (e.g., specific downstream accuracy or unsupported quant path), budget for multi-GPU replicas (plan 3 GPUs per replica). For your QPS and HA profile, start with 3 replicas (9x80GB) and autoscale for spikes.
- If you can accept a validated 4-bit quantized variant (we can run evals on your prompt set), we can fit a replica on a single 80GB GPU. That reduces Dedicated pool size dramatically — start with 3 single-GPU replicas (3x80GB) and provision headroom (1–2 GPUs) for bursts.

I'll loop Marcus for a technical breakdown with explicit per-GPU allocation numbers and a sample spreadsheet. Also: we should run a short quantization eval on your prompt set to validate quality regressions — happy to coordinate.

—Logan

Adding the technical breakdown and the attached workbook (vitali-v1-sizing.xlsx) so procurement and infra can see explicit math. Highlights from my side:

- Weight footprint (illustrative):
  • FP16: 70B * 2B = ~140 GB (resident).
  • int8 (symmetric): ~70–80 GB.
  • 4-bit (LLM.quant variants): ~40–55 GB depending on quant method and any per-layer residuals.

- KV cache: my calc uses 0.9 KB/token baseline -> 32k tokens ~= 29 MB. Note this is per-active-request. So 100 concurrent active long sessions would mean ~2.9 GB just in KV. This is why concurrency and session churn matter for sizing.

- Activation scratch + runtime overhead: plan an additional 10–30% above weights to cover attention buffers, fused kernels, and batch headroom. For FP16, that pushes the per-replica resident memory into the ~180–200 GB ballpark. For quantized variants, the overhead is lower but still non-zero.

- Example pool mapping (sustained 4 r/s, avg 512 tokens, peak bursts to 12 r/s):
  Scenario A — FP16 replicas:
    • Replica config: 3x A100/H100 80GB (model-sharded).
    • Start: 3 replicas for HA = 9 GPUs.
    • Autoscale: +2 GPUs to absorb 12 r/s bursts / increased concurrency (policy: scale at >6 queued requests).
  Scenario B — 4-bit quant replicas:
    • Replica config: 1x A100/H100 80GB per replica.
    • Start: 3 replicas = 3 GPUs.
    • Autoscale: +1–2 GPUs for burst headroom.

- Notes on latency: quantized single-GPU replicas typically have slightly higher per-token decode throughput in CPU-bound parts due to dequant costs, but they remove cross-GPU syncs which often improves p95 latency for interactive loads. We'll provide p50/p95 estimates once we run a short benchmark with your sample sessions.

Attachments included: vitali-v1-sizing.xlsx (sheet: replica-maps & cost-ops), kv-cache-estimates.csv (token distribution sample).

I'll schedule a quick 30-min tech call if you want to walk through the sheet — ping me with availability.
